meta.model: ArtaMatch quality — oriented toward happy, Lasso-selected, non-negative

rules.name: his_pluto_square_her_neptune
rules.human: His Pluto challenges her Neptune
rules.what: His Pluto is depth, power and the things that transform a person. Her Neptune is dreams, compassion and the blur between two souls. Synastry reads this contact as one of the live wires between two people.
rules.how: Laying his birth chart over hers, his Pluto and her Neptune sit 90° apart — friction that forces both people to grow.

rules.name: NOT(cyclephase_uranus_neptune=DisseminatingxDisseminating)
rules.human: Not: Both born in the Disseminating phase of Uranus–Neptune
rules.what: Rudhyar read every planetary pair as a cycle with the same eight phases the Moon has — new, crescent, first quarter, gibbous, full, disseminating, last quarter, balsamic. The phase says where in a long story a birth falls: the new phase begins something, the full illuminates it, the balsamic lets it go. Here it is its ABSENCE that the model reads, which is the same doctrine stated the other way round.
rules.how: This condition does NOT hold. Measure the angle from Neptune to Uranus and read it as a lunation: his birth falls in the Disseminating phase, hers in the Disseminating.

rules.name: his_jupiter_square_her_venus

rules.how: Laying his birth chart over hers, his Jupiter and her Venus sit 90° apart — friction that forces both people to grow.

rules.name: NOT(compX_sun_semisext_venus)

rules.what: The Sun is who someone is at the core — vitality, pride, the will to shine; Venus is love, affection, beauty and what someone treasures. This is an aspect the RELATIONSHIP carries, not one either person brought to it. Here it is its ABSENCE that the model reads, which is the same doctrine stated the other way round.
rules.how: This condition does NOT hold. In the composite chart — the midpoint of the two birth charts, read as the relationship itself, the Sun and Venus sit 30° apart — a small, persistent adjustment.

rules.name: NOT(herlotmarriage_his_lot_marriage_trine_her_mars)

rules.tradition: Classical astrology — the Lot of Marriage
rules.what: The Arabic parts are computed points rather than bodies, and the Lot of Marriage is the one classical astrology reads a union from. Mars is desire, drive and the way a person fights. Here it is its ABSENCE that the model reads, which is the same doctrine stated the other way round.
rules.how: This condition does NOT hold. The Lot of Marriage is cast from the ascendant, its opposite point and Venus. His lot and her Mars sit 120° apart — the easiest angle in astrology, help given freely.

rules.what: Tara is read for fortune between the two — some counts are auspicious, and the 3rd, 5th and 7th are the ones the tradition warns about.
rules.how: Counting from his birth star to hers and back again gives the Tara pair.

rules.name: guna_total_band=3
rules.human: Guna Milan score 24–27 out of 36
rules.what: This is the number a Vedic astrologer actually gives a couple. Eighteen of thirty-six is the classical threshold for a match; the high twenties is considered a strong one.
rules.how: The eight traditional compatibility tests, scored and added: Varna, Vashya, Tara, Yoni, Graha Maitri, Gana, Bhakoot and Nadi.

rules.name: nadipair=MadhyaxMadhya
rules.human: His nadi Madhya, hers Madhya
rules.what: Nadi is the constitutional pulse. Both of you carry Pitta — fire and drive. Different nadis score the full eight points; the same nadi scores nothing.
rules.how: His birth star falls in the Madhya nadi, hers in the Madhya nadi.

rules.name: dav_mode_Fixed_count=2
rules.human: 2 bodies in Fixed in the Davison chart
rules.what: Counting the elements is the first thing a reader does with any chart. Fixed is holding on; a chart heavy or empty in one of them is read as leaning that way.
rules.how: Of the ten bodies in the relationship's own chart, 2 fall in Fixed.

rules.how: Both birth stars fall in the same nadi, so the koota scores zero of eight.
